summary: Substack validates the list-endpoint limit server-side and fails the whole resource when it is exceeded, so the generic sync page size has to be clamped per resource rather than taken from the spec. The caps are not uniform across endpoints and are re-measurable, so a reprint must probe them again rather than restore a single spec-derived page size.
reason: The page size the generator derives sits above what Substack accepts: any limit past the cap returns HTTP 400 {"errors":[{"location":"query","param":"limit","value":N,"msg":"Invalid value"}]}, which fails drafts, posts, and posts-published outright instead of degrading the page. /post_management/published caps lower than the other list endpoints, so one shared value is not enough and the clamp is keyed by resource. The clamp is applied to paginationDefaults.limit at its single point of use because that one value drives the request limit, the short-page stop check, and the offset stride together; lowering only the request limit would leave the stride skipping past unread records.
validated_outcome: Measured live against www.thefp.com and astralcodexten.substack.com: /api/v1/archive returns 200 at limit=50 and HTTP 400 at limit=51+. End-to-end against astralcodexten, the pre-fix binary failed the posts resource with sync_error status 400 and total_records 0; the patched binary synced the resource successfully. Note for a future reprint: these resources still fetch only their first page, because extractPageItems reports hasMore=false for the bare JSON arrays these endpoints return — a separate defect from this limit cap, tracked upstream.
